Obstacle

/OB-stuh-kul/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Obstacle means something that blocks or hinders progress, movement, or achievement

Obstacle means something that stands in the way of progress or movement. A rockslide left a pile of boulders across the mountain road — an obstacle no car could get past.

Worked Example

The biggest obstacle to the vaccine campaign was distance: many villages lay a full day's walk from the nearest clinic.

Nothing physical is lying in the road here — distance itself is what blocks the goal. An obstacle can be any condition that stands between you and what you're trying to achieve, not just a physical object.

How Obstacle Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

hindrance

hindrance: something that makes progress harder

impediment

impediment: something that delays or blocks movement or action

hurdle

hurdle: a difficulty that must be gotten over to move forward

Antonyms

advantage

advantage: a condition that helps you succeed

boost

boost: something that pushes progress forward

How Strong Is It? — snag → obstacle → impasse

snag vs. obstacle

snag vs. obstacle: A snag is a small hitch that slows you down for a moment; an obstacle genuinely blocks your path until you deal with it.

impasse vs. obstacle

impasse vs. obstacle: An impasse is stronger than an obstacle — progress doesn't just get blocked, it stops completely, with no way forward in sight.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of obstacle.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — ob-

Prefix — ob-: against, in the way (Latin)

Root — sta

Root — sta: to stand (Latin stare)

Suffix — -cle

Suffix — -cle: a thing that (noun-forming ending)

Put it together

Put it together: An obstacle is literally 'a thing that stands against you' — ob- (in the way) plus the Latin root stare (to stand): something standing squarely in your path.

Use the root in a new word: obstinate

Use the root in a new word: obstinate: Despite every counterargument, the committee chair remained obstinate and refused to move the deadline.

Root Check

Word Choice

Neutral

You overcome, remove, or face an obstacle, and something is an obstacle to a goal: 'an obstacle to peace,' 'an obstacle to progress.' It can be physical (a fallen tree) or abstract (fear, cost, distance) — and an obstacle course strings physical ones together on purpose.
